thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call — auth-service token verification error spike (high severity). Alert: token_verif_errors > 10% for 5m. Root: external IdP responses failing

alex: seeing large number of login failures and console 401/500s since ~14:22 UTC. Dashboards show heavy 502/504s from Okta introspect and intermittent jwks 403s. Customers reporting console lockouts.

maria: acknowledged. I'm oncall. grabbing logs now. Which path is failing more, user login or console sessions?

kevin: user-login spikes highest, but console admin auth is affected too — we see 12-15% of tokens failing verification. Rate of introspect calls returning 502 from Okta.

sara: status page (okta) shows partial outage in region EU-W. Link: https://status.okta.com/incident/12345 (reported 14:18 UTC)

status-bot: Okta incident updated: Customer-impacting — token introspect API degraded in EU-W. (https://status.okta.com)

maria: action plan: 1) reduce fanout to introspect by enabling local trust for cached JWKS for short window, 2) enable console fallback auth for Redwood staff using internal SSO bypass, 3) open ticket with Okta and request ETA. I'll coordinate.

alex: +1. For 1) we can switch the verification library to use cached keys for 10m if remote jwks fails. Patch ready in prod-config: 
```yaml
auth: 
  jwks_cache_ttl: 600 # secs temporary override
  jwks_strict_fail: false # allow cached when remote fails
```

kevin: how do we flip that safely? Can we feature-flag it at runtime?

maria: yes, we have a runtime flag. Rolling to 2% canary first then 100% in 5m. I'll start canary.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: auth-introspect-degradation v2 — steps: 1) enable jwks-cache-fallback 2) enable console-admin-bypass 3) notify product & support 4) monitor token_verif_errors metric

alex: starting canary now. Command: 
```bash
# enable jwks cache fallback via config service
curl -X POST "https://config.internal/api/v1/flags/auth.jwks_cache_fallback" -d '{"value":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CFG_TOKEN'
```

maria: canary started (2% traffic). Observing metrics...

kevin: token_verif_errors dropped to ~6% in canary after 90s. Good signal.

maria: bumping to 50% now.

sara: Support: Customer impact: approx 8% of login attempts failing globally, concentrated EU-W and some NA. Ticket template being posted to support channels, sending customer advisory: "We're aware of Okta token introspect degradation causing login failures; working on a mitigation."

alex: I've also enabled console admin bypass for SRE so we can access affected consoles to troubleshoot. Command: 
```bash
# short-lived admin bypass for consoles
rbacctl grant --role temporary-admin --subject group:sre --duration 30m
```

maria: rolling to 100% jwks-cache-fallback now. Monitoring closely.

kevin: downstream: some customers using short-lived sessions may see session mismatch until tokens rotate. Communicating to CSM to pause critical login-dependent flows.

status-bot: Okta status updated: "Investigating — degraded performance for /introspect" (14:35 UTC)

maria: 10m after 100% roll, token_verif_errors back to baseline (~0.5%), console access restored for staff. We will hold mitigation for 20m then revert.

alex: good. Opened Okta support case ID: OKTA-98765, linked logs and request for root cause and ETA for fix.

sara: Posted incident note to customers@ with temporary workaround and ETA placeholder.

maria: escalation notes: 1) add alert for jwks_fetch_errors 2) improve cached-jwks fallback test coverage 3) run failover drills for IdP outages. Owner: alex, due EOD next week.

kevin: follow-up: add circuit-breaker to introspect path to reduce blast radius and add sampling for full token payloads to debug future issues (PII redaction).

ops-runbook-bot: Incident ack recorded. Severity: Sev2. Duration: 14:22 UTC - 14:52 UTC. Postmortem scheduled.

maria: handing off to incident review channel. Thanks all for quick response. :thumbsup:
